title: Observation of a Rydberg-atom time crystal with an ultralong lifetime
authors: Qi-Feng Wang, Tian-Yu Han, Ya-Jun Wang, Dong-Yang Zhu, Chao Yu, Yu Ma, Yi-Ming Yin, Guang-Can Guo, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Dong-Sheng Ding, Bao-Sen Shi
abstract: Continuous time crystals (CTCs) represent a nonequilibrium quantum phase that spontaneously breaks time-translation symmetry without periodic external driving, manifesting as persistent, long-lived oscillations under steady pumping. The lifetime is constrained by the instability of the limit cycle phase, balanced between nonlinear feedback and energy dissipation, which have rarely been studied in experiments before. Here, we report an observation of an ultralong-lived Rydberg-atom CTC in a driven-dissipative many-body atomic system. By harnessing long-range interactions and engineering a dissipative environment that stabilizes the limit-cycle dynamics, we suppress heating and decay effects that typically destroy time-crystalline order. The key factor underlying the ultralong-lived CTC is the closing of the Liouvillian gap and the near-zero real part of the system's Liouvillian eigenspectrum. Through systematic optimization, we achieve an oscillatory lifetime exceeding 16.95 hours-orders of magnitude longer than previous CTC realizations. Our work establishes a robust platform for exploring long-lived autonomous nonequilibrium phases and paves the way for applications in quantum sensing and continuous-time quantum information processing.
summary: The researchers successfully observed a Continuous Time Crystal (CTC) using Rydberg atoms, achieving an unprecedentedly long lifetime exceeding 16.95 hours. They achieved this by engineering the dissipative environment to stabilize the system's limit-cycle dynamics against typical decay mechanisms. This work establishes a powerful platform for studying robust, autonomous non-equilibrium quantum phases.
main_problem: The primary goal is observing and understanding Continuous Time Crystals (CTCs), which are non-equilibrium quantum phases that spontaneously break time-translation symmetry without periodic external driving.
main_result: The authors reported the observation of an ultralong-lived Rydberg-atom CTC with a lifetime exceeding 16.95 hours, significantly surpassing previous realizations.
method: The study uses theoretical analysis based on the Lindblad master equation and experimental measurements involving controlled optical pumping and external RF fields to stabilize the limit-cycle dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is a Rydberg-atom ensemble interacting via long-range van der Waals forces, driven by coherent laser/RF fields in a dissipative environment. The dynamics are modeled using the Lindblad master equation.
key_observables: CTC behavior (persistent oscillations), oscillatory lifetime ($	au_l$), and onset time ($	au_o$).
important_parameters: External RF field amplitude ($E$) and laser detuning ($\Delta_c$); achieving a near-zero real part of the Liouvillian eigenspectrum is key.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a mean-field treatment, which neglects inter-atomic correlations due to atomic thermal motion.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate system diagrams, energy level structures, time evolution simulations under varying decay rates, and plots showing measured CTC criticality and lifetime dependence on applied electric field amplitude or laser detuning.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the concept of CTCs, details the theoretical framework using the Lindblad master equation and Liouvillian spectrum analysis, presents experimental measurements demonstrating the long-lived limit cycle phase, and concludes by establishing a robust platform for studying autonomous non-equilibrium phases.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it pushes the boundaries of open quantum systems physics by experimentally realizing and stabilizing an exotic, non-equilibrium quantum phase (DTC) in a controllable atomic platform (Rydberg atoms).
